original_question: Find the asymptotic value of D(3,n) when the three distinguished points are not collinear, where D(3,n) asks for the minimum number of distances determined between those three points and another set of n points.
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 20: the bipartite distinct-distances problem asking for the asymptotic value of D(3,n) in the non-collinear three-point case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact open problem: the asymptotic behavior of D(3,n) for three non-collinear points against an n-point set, i.e. the non-collinear three-point bipartite distinct-distances question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
missing_details: The ambient space is the Euclidean plane R^2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

D(3,n) is a minimum over all choices of two planar point sets P1,P2 with |P1|=3 and |P2|=n; it is not a question about one fixed preselected triple of points. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

The three points are required to form a non-collinear set P1; this is the paper's exact hypothesis, not merely 'distinguished points' in an informal sense. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

Only cross-distances are counted, namely distances |pq| with p in P1 and q in P2; distances within P1 or within P2 are irrelevant. This is the paper's bipartite-distance convention. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
The question asks for the asymptotic growth rate as n→∞ of the minimum possible number of such distinct cross-distances. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

The paper does not state extra conditions such as general position for P2 or disjointness of P1 and P2, so a faithful restatement should not introduce them. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
refined_question: For Euclidean distance in R^2, let D(3,n)=min |{||p-q|| : p∈P1, q∈P2}|, where the minimum is over all point sets P1,P2⊂R^2 with |P1|=3, |P2|=n, and P1 non-collinear. Only distances between a point of P1 and a point of P2 are counted. Determine the asymptotic growth rate of D(3,n) as n→∞.
justification: This is the exact narrow problem the paper isolates in its bipartite-distances section. The section first sets the bipartite convention that only distances arising from pairs in P1×P2 are counted, and then specializes to the case of three points versus n points. In the current arXiv version this appears as Section 5, Problem 20; the accompanying paragraph defines D(3,n) as the minimum number of distinct distances between a set P1 of three non-collinear points and a set P2 of n points in R^2. Your draft is therefore very close, but it should explicitly encode the minimization over both sets, the planar Euclidean setting, and the fact that only cross-distances are counted. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
